this_repository.gpu_policy: portable Mojo first; vendor specialization only when justified
this_repository.legacy_cpp_cuda: removed; do not reintroduce project-owned C++/CUDA
do_not_fake: nightly-only APIs in stable code without an explicit feature/toolchain note
hardware targets not supported by the installed Mojo version
a native Mojo package-manager workflow that the pinned toolchain does not provide
CUDA C++/HIP source as the default GPU implementation
C++26/XMake/CMake requirements inherited from the old implementation

dependency_environment.rule: Use the repository's existing environment manager. Do not introduce an additional manager without reason.

toolchain.accelerator_targeting: Use only --target-accelerator values verified by the installed version/current stable docs.

language_policy.strong_typing: Prefer explicit types for public APIs and performance-critical code.

principles: do not reproduce C++ header/module architecture mechanically

ownership.principle: Ownership, mutability, lifetime, and resource cleanup must be explicit.

argument_and_reference_conventions.read: prefer for immutable borrowed access when appropriate
argument_and_reference_conventions.mut: use for mutable borrowed access when appropriate
argument_and_reference_conventions.ref: use for named references when a copy is not intended
argument_and_reference_conventions.var_or_owned: use when ownership transfer/consumption is intentional

ownership.origins_and_lifetimes: Treat origin/lifetime correctness as part of API design.

pointers.unsafe: unsafe_ operations only in isolated, justified, bounded, tested low-level code
pointers.manual_allocation: only for low-level structures, FFI, or measured hot paths

destruction.automatic: __deinit__(deinit self) when custom automatic cleanup is required
destruction.explicit: @explicit_destroy when cleanup is ordered, selectable, expensive, or may fail

resource_management.rule: Every resource must have a deterministic destruction path.

avoid: unnecessary dynamic Python objects in hot paths

principles: keep domain logic separate from hardware-specific optimization

avoid: scalar hot loops when a verified SIMD implementation is appropriate

allowed_hardware: Apple when supported by the installed toolchain
gpu.rule: Hardware-specific code must stay behind a Mojo interface and be justified by measurement or a hard platform constraint.

allowed_for: dependencies without a suitable Mojo path
python.hot_path_rule: Do not move performance-critical Mojo code to Python merely for implementation convenience.

c.rule: Keep the boundary narrow and explicit.

cpp.default: do not introduce as project implementation language
cpp.exception: only when an unavoidable third-party/platform constraint has no suitable Mojo/C/Python boundary

principles: prefer zero-cost or compile-time specialization where useful
separate algorithmic improvements from hardware-specific tuning

requirements: bug fixes should include regression tests when practical
compare CPU/GPU and available vendor backends when applicable
state hardware and input shape when reporting results
do not claim one backend is faster without reproducible evidence

formatting.rule: Format changed Mojo source files before considering the change complete.

requirements: validate lengths, shapes, strides, and bounds
check integer conversions where overflow/truncation matters
treat unsafe_ operations as audited low-level code

policy: prefer stable Mojo standard-library functionality when adequate
inspect existing dependencies before adding alternatives
avoid duplicate libraries solving the same concern
pin or constrain dependencies when reproducibility matters

avoid: comments that merely restate obvious code

per_component_process: define idiomatic Mojo API from the spec
implement in Mojo rather than transliterating other languages
validate numerical equivalence when multiple backends exist

before_modification: read every .md in .cursor/specs/ except README.md and files starting with _
inspect relevant existing source and tests
verify unstable or unfamiliar Mojo/MAX APIs
during_modification: keep portable GPU logic separate from vendor specialization
after_modification: run or recommend relevant Mojo tests
verify CPU/GPU numerical behavior when relevant
benchmark performance-sensitive changes when required by the spec

forbidden_defaults: Do not create project-owned C++/CUDA/HIP/Triton implementations.
Do not introduce XMake/CMake/Make/Meson for Mojo source.
Do not use legacy fn syntax.
Do not hallucinate Mojo or MAX APIs.
Do not use nightly-only features silently in stable code.
Do not use unsafe_ memory operations without a narrow justification.
Do not add hardware-specific specialization before a portable implementation unless the spec requires it.

exceptions.rule: A rule may be overridden only by an explicit spec/user instruction, interoperability/platform constraint, or measured performance requirement.
require: preserve safety and portability where possible
add tests/benchmarks appropriate to the exception
